question: What is the universal root superclass of every class in the Java type system?

options.text: Classes without an explicit extends clause have no superclass whatsoever.
java.lang.Throwable, which provides core heap memory layout rules.
java.lang.Class, which acts as the meta-root for all class types.
java.lang.Object, from which all Java classes ultimately descend.

explanation: In Java, java.lang.Object is the root of the class hierarchy. Every class that does not explicitly extend another class implicitly extends Object.

question: Can a Java class directly inherit implementation from more than one superclass using `extends A, B`?

options.text: Yes, provided the extended classes opt out of inheriting from java.lang.Object.
Yes, classes can inherit from multiple parent classes if they share common roots.
No, unless all constructors in the parent classes are explicitly bypassed.
No, Java supports only single inheritance of class implementations.

explanation: Java enforces single inheritance for classes: a class can extend at most one direct superclass, preventing multiple-inheritance state conflicts.

question: What happens when an object of a subclass is instantiated regarding the superclass constructor?

options.text: The superclass constructor is completely skipped because the subclass replaces it.
The superclass constructor executes first to initialize inherited superclass state.
The superclass constructor runs only if downcasting is performed on the reference.
The superclass constructor is executed asynchronously after the subclass completes.

explanation: Object initialization proceeds from superclass to subclass. The superclass constructor must execute (via super()) before subclass constructor statements run.

question: If Dog and Cat both directly extend Animal, can a Dog reference be cast directly to Cat?

options.text: No, sibling classes in the hierarchy are unrelated and cannot be cast to each other.
Yes, sibling classes share the same parent and can be cast to each other freely.
Yes, provided Animal opts out of the java.lang.Object hierarchy.
Yes, downcasting across siblings is always safe because both descend from Animal.

explanation: Sibling classes share a common superclass but do not have an IS-A relationship with each other. Attempting to cast between sibling classes fails compile-time or runtime type checks.

question: Is assigning a subclass instance to a superclass reference variable (upcasting) safe without an explicit cast?

options.text: No, because upcasting skips the execution of superclass constructor methods.
No, upcasting causes compile errors unless an explicit cast operator is used.
Yes, upcasting is always type-safe and performed implicitly by the compiler.
Yes, but only for classes that explicitly opt out of extending Object.

explanation: Upcasting (widening reference conversion) is always safe because an instance of a subclass IS-A instance of its superclass, so no explicit cast is needed.

question: Can a Java class opt out of extending java.lang.Object in its declaration?

options.text: No, every Java class extends Object directly or through its inheritance chain.
Yes, abstract classes never descend from java.lang.Object.
Yes, classes can opt out of extending java.lang.Object using native modifiers.
Yes, sibling classes are exempt from extending Object if they share a package.

explanation: It is impossible for a class in Java to avoid extending java.lang.Object. Even if not specified, the compiler enforces Object as the ultimate root superclass.
